newsitem.title: FRANCE: World Bank official has talks on Algeria reforms.
newsitem.headline: World Bank official has talks on Algeria reforms.

text.p: The World Bank's deputy head for North Africa and the Middle East, Kamal Dervis, held talks with Algerian ministers on the country's economic performance and cooperation with the bank, Algerian television said on Thursday.
It quoted Dervis as saying that he met Finance Minister Abdelkrim Harchaoui, who briefed him on economic reforms and the 1997 budget.
"We intend to pursue cooperation with Algeria to spur investment and job creation," the television reported him as saying.
Dervis on Wednesday met Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and Ali Hamdi, junior minister for planning. It was Dervis's fourth visit to the North African country in 1996.
Algeria's appointed quasi-parliament, the Transitional National Council, this week approved an 84.7 billion dinars ($1.54 billion) budget deficit for 1997.
The government has said the budget is intended to stimulate investment and improve production through fiscal incentives like corporate cuts in value-added tax.
The government is striving to shift the economy to free-market rules under a three-year accord with the International Monetary Fund that began in 1995.
The reforms began showing results with more than four percent growth in gross domestic product in 1995 and the first half of 1996, reversing falls in 1993 and 1994.

Authorities have been locked in a five-year conflict with radical Moslem fundamentalists whose ranks, according to officials, have been reinforced in recent years by young people frustrated by a 28 percent jobless rate and a housing crisis.
